headlines.title: Hackers targeted municipal water systems in 7 states this week, FBI says
headlines.description: Cyberattacks targeting municipal water systems have been reported in at least seven states this week, prompting the FBI and the Environmental Protection Agency to warn utilities nationwide that hackers are trying to disrupt critical water infrastructure.

headlines.title: Judge denies request by Elon Musk’s xAI to pause Minnesota nudification ban
headlines.description: A judge denied a request from Elon Musk’s AI company xAI to block Minnesota’s law that will be the first in the nation to ban nudification technology.

headlines.title: Trump Says Iran Talks to Resume After Strikes Called off
headlines.description: President Donald Trump announced the United States and Iran are set to resume talks following his decision to call off massive strikes over the weekend. There’s no confirmation from Iran but Iran’s foreign minister did say, “Negotiations are on the path to being finalized.” NBC’s Keir Simmons reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: Israel says it has concerns with Hamas disarmament deal as it keeps up Gaza strikes
headlines.description: Israel says it has shared concerns with the United States about the proposed disarmament deal with Hamas, raising new doubts about the agreement touted by President Donald Trump.

headlines.title: Blanche Scraps ‘Anti-Weaponization’ Fund Ahead of Nomination
headlines.description: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche’s nomination appears to be back on track after he announced a key decision to satisfy two Republican holdouts in the Senate who said they could not support his confirmation until the “anti-weaponization” fund was rescinded in writing. Now, Blanche posted an order establishing, “Beyond any doubt, there is no fund.” NBC’s Garrett Haake reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: Michigan reports first two deaths in the cyclosporiasis outbreak
headlines.description: Two people in Michigan who had contracted cyclosporiasis have died, the state Health and Human Services Department said Monday.

headlines.title: Urgent warning over water system cyberattacks
headlines.description: The Trump administration is warning about potential cyberattacks after a senior law enforcement official told NBC News that a cyberattack on water systems in Minnesota had all the hallmarks of Iranian-backed hackers. NBC News’ Garrett Haake reports.

headlines.title: How ‘cigfluencers’ are bringing back smoking on social media against doctors’ orders
headlines.description: Despite medical research, some content creators say cigarettes are back in fashion. "Cigfluencers" are making waves online as Hollywood and magazines seem to embrace the old habit. NBC News' Dr. Akshay Syal reports.

headlines.title: OpenAI's rogue AI hacking of several companies opens new cybersecurity questions
headlines.description: OpenAI revealed that its AI agent tried to hack several other companies after hacking into Hugging Face. Juan Andrés Guerrero-Saade, Sentinelone's VP of intelligence and security research, joins NBC News' Garrett Haake to discuss whether Congress can regulate the pace of AI growth and the future of cybersecurity amid AI hackers.

headlines.title: FCC chair defends new U.S. ban on foreign-made humanoid robots, a market China dominates
headlines.description: The Trump administration will ban foreign-made humanoid robots in the U.S. as China seeks to dominate the emerging high-tech market. Speaking to NBC News, the FCC chair Brendan Carr defends the move. NBC News' Kelly O'Donnell reports.

headlines.title: American Airlines lifts nationwide ground stop
headlines.description: An American Airlines' nationwide ground stop caused by technology has now been lifted, but could cause further issues with delayed flights. NBC News’ Jay Blackman explains.

headlines.title: Company releases video of moth-killing drone aimed at curbing mosquito population
headlines.description: Tech start-up TORNYOL released a video of its "first air-to-air kill" mini-drone and says it could kill mosquitoes "at an unprecedented scale and cost." But experts say swatting the bugs away could be more complicated. NBC News' Marquise Francis reports.
